title.zh: 卷七十六 列傳第六: 耶律解里 耶律拔里得 耶律朔古 耶律魯不古 趙延壽 高模翰 趙思溫 耶律漚里思 張礪
title.en: Volume 76 Biographies 6: Yelu Jieli, Yelu Balide, Yelu Shuogu, Yelu Lubugu, Zhao Yanshou, Gao Mohan, Zhao Siwen, Yelu Oulisi, Zhang Li
title.raw: 卷七十六 列傳第六: 耶律解里 耶律拔里得 耶律朔古 耶律魯不古 趙延壽 高模翰 趙思溫 耶律漚里思 張礪 Volume 76 Biographies 6: Yelu Jieli, Yelu Balide, Yelu Shuogu, Yelu Lubugu, Zhao Yanshou, Gao Mohan, Zhao Siwen, Yelu Oulisi, Zhang Li

sentences.zh: 耶律解裏耶律拔裏得耶律朔古耶律魯不古趙延壽高模翰趙思溫耶律漚裏思張礪

translations.literal: Yelu Jieli, Yelu Balide, Yelu Shuogu, Yelu Lubugu, Zhao Yanshou, Gao Mohan, Zhao Siwen, Yelu Oulisi, Zhang Li
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Jieli, Yelu Balide, Yelu Shuogu, Yelu Lubugu, Zhao Yanshou, Gao Mohan, Zhao Siwen, Yelu Oulisi, and Zhang Li

sentences.zh: 耶律解裏，字潑單，突呂不部人，世為小吏。

translations.literal: Yelu Jieli, courtesy name Podan, was a man of the Tulubu tribe; his family had served for generations as minor clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Jieli, whose courtesy name was Podan, came from the Tulubu tribe; for generations his family had held low clerical posts.

sentences.zh: 解裏早隸太宗麾下，擢為軍校。

translations.literal: Jieli early entered service under Emperor Taizong and was promoted to military instructor.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli entered Taizong's service while still young and was eventually promoted to the rank of military instructor.

sentences.zh: 天顯間，唐攻定州，既陷，解裏為唐兵所獲。

translations.literal: During the Tianxian era, Tang attacked Dingzhou; after it fell, Jieli was captured by Tang troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianxian period, when Tang forces attacked and captured Dingzhou, Jieli was taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 晉高祖立，始歸國。

translations.literal: When Jin Emperor Gaozu was established, he at last returned to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Emperor Gaozu of Jin came to the throne did he return to Liao.

sentences.zh: 太宗貰其罪，拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: Taizong pardoned his offense and appointed him Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong forgave his lapse and appointed him Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 會同九年伐晉，師次滹沱河，奪中渡橋，降其將杜重威。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Huitong he campaigned against Jin; the army halted at the Hutuo River, seized the Zhongdu Bridge, and reduced the Jin general Du Chongwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Huitong, on the campaign against Jin, the army encamped at the Hutuo River, took the Zhongdu Bridge, and compelled the surrender of the Jin commander Du Chongwei.

sentences.zh: 上命解裏與降將張彥澤率騎兵三千疾趨河南，所至無敢當其鋒。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Jieli and the surrendered general Zhang Yanze to lead three thousand horsemen in a rapid advance into Henan; wherever they went none dared meet their charge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jieli and the surrendered general Zhang Yanze to ride south into Henan at the head of three thousand cavalry; nowhere along their route did anyone dare stand against them.

sentences.zh: 既入汴，解裏等遷晉主重貴於開封府。

translations.literal: After entering Bian, Jieli and the others moved the Jin ruler Chonggui to the Kaifeng prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had entered Bian, Jieli and his colleagues transferred the Jin emperor Chonggui to the Kaifeng prefectural residence.

sentences.zh: 彥澤恣殺掠，亂宮掖，解裏不能禁，百姓騷然，莫不怨憤。

translations.literal: Yanze indulged in killing and plunder, throwing the palace quarters into disorder; Jieli could not restrain him, and the people were in uproar, all filled with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yanze ran wild with slaughter and looting and threw the inner palace into chaos; Jieli was unable to stop him, and the populace seethed with universal outrage.

sentences.zh: 車駕至京，數彥澤罪，斬於市，汴人大悅。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached the capital, the emperor enumerated Yanze's crimes and had him executed in the marketplace; the people of Bian were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived in the capital, he recited Yanze's crimes and had him beheaded in the market; the people of Bian rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 解裏亦被詰責，尋釋之。

translations.literal: Jieli was also called to account, but was soon released.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli was rebuked as well, though he was released shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 天祿間，加守太子太傅。

translations.literal: During the Tianlu era he was given the additional title of Guardian Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianlu period he was additionally appointed Guardian Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 應歷初，置本部令穩，解裏世其職，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingli the post of tribal commander Wen was established; Jieli held the office by hereditary succession and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yingli reign the post of tribal commander Wen was created; Jieli inherited the office in succession and died while serving.

sentences.zh: 耶律拔裏得，字孩鄰，太祖弟剌葛之子。

translations.literal: Yelu Balide, courtesy name Hailin, was a son of Emperor Taizu's younger brother Yelu Dilie.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Balide, whose courtesy name was Hailin, was the son of Taizu's younger brother Yelu Dilie.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，以親愛見任。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Balide was trusted because of their close kinship.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, Balide won his trust through their close family bond.

sentences.zh: 會同七年，討石重貴，拔裏得進圍德州，下之，擒刺史師居璠等二十七人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Huitong, campaigning against Shi Chonggui, Balide advanced to besiege Dezhou, took it, and captured the prefect Shi Jufan and twenty-seven others.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Huitong, on the expedition against Shi Chonggui, Balide pressed the siege of Dezhou, captured the city, and took the prefect Shi Jufan and twenty-seven others prisoner.

sentences.zh: 九年，再舉兵，次滹沱河，降杜重威，戰功居多。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he took the field again, halted at the Hutuo River, and reduced Du Chongwei; his battle achievements were foremost among the commanders.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he marched again, encamped at the Hutuo River, and helped bring about Du Chongwei's surrender; among the generals his share of the fighting was the greatest.

sentences.zh: 太宗入汴，以功授安國軍節度使，總領河北道事。

translations.literal: When Taizong entered Bian, Balide was made Military Governor of Anguo for his merit and given overall charge of affairs on the Hebei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong entered Bian, Balide was appointed Military Governor of Anguo in recognition of his service and placed in overall charge of the Hebei circuit.

sentences.zh: 師還，州郡往往叛，以應劉知遠，拔裏得不能守而歸。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, prefectures and districts often rebelled to join Liu Zhiyuan; Balide could not hold his post and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's withdrawal, one prefecture after another rose in revolt to answer Liu Zhiyuan; Balide could not maintain his position and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遷中京留守，卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong came to the throne, Balide was transferred to be garrison commander of the Central Capital and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong's accession he was transferred to serve as garrison commander of the Central Capital, where he died.

sentences.zh: 耶律魯不古，字信寧，太祖從侄也。

translations.literal: Yelu Lubugu, courtesy name Xinning, was a younger cousin of Emperor Taizu on the father's side.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Lubugu, whose courtesy name was Xinning, was a younger cousin of Taizu on the paternal line.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖制契丹國字，魯不古以贊成功，授林牙、監修國史。

translations.literal: When Taizu first devised the Khitan national script, Lubugu assisted in the achievement and was appointed Yelu (chancellor) and Supervisor of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu first created the Khitan national script, Lubugu helped bring the project to completion and was appointed chancellor and supervisor of the compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 後率偏師，為西南邊大詳穩，從伐党項有功。

translations.literal: Later he led a detached force as Grand Commander of the southwestern frontier and rendered merit in campaigns against the Tanguts.
translations.idiomatic: He later commanded a detached force as grand commander of the southwestern frontier and distinguished himself in campaigns against the Tanguts.

sentences.zh: 會河東節度使石敬瑭為其主所討，遣人求援，魯不古導送於朝，如其請。

translations.literal: When Hedong Military Governor Shi Jingtang was attacked by his sovereign and sent envoys to seek aid, Lubugu guided them to court and conveyed their request, which was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hedong military governor Shi Jingtang was attacked by his own ruler and sent envoys to plead for help, Lubugu escorted them to court and presented their request, which the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 帝親率師往援，魯不古從擊唐將張敬達於太原北，敗之。

translations.literal: The emperor personally led troops to the rescue; Lubugu followed and struck the Tang general Zhang Jingda north of Taiyuan, defeating him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched in person to relieve him; Lubugu took part in the attack on the Tang commander Zhang Jingda north of Taiyuan and routed his army.

sentences.zh: 會同初，從討党項，俘獲最諸將，師還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong he joined the campaign against the Tanguts; his captives and booty exceeded those of all other generals, and the army returned.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huitong era he joined the expedition against the Tanguts and took more prisoners and booty than any other commander before the army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 天祿中，拜於越。

translations.literal: During the Tianlu era he was invested as Yuyue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianlu period he received the title of Yuyue.

sentences.zh: 六年，為北院大王。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he became Great King of the Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Great King of the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 終年五十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽，本姓劉，恒山人。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou, original surname Liu, was a native of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou, whose original surname was Liu, came from Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 父邟，令蓚。

translations.literal: His father Kuang was magistrate of Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kuang had served as magistrate of Shuo.

sentences.zh: 梁開平初，滄州節度使劉守文陷蓚，其稗將趙德鈞獲延壽，養以為子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Liang Kaiping, Cangzhou Military Governor Liu Shouwen seized Shuo; his subordinate general Zhao Dejun captured Yanshou and raised him as a son.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Liang Kaiping era, when the military governor of Cangzhou, Liu Shouwen, overran Shuo, his lieutenant Zhao Dejun took Yanshou prisoner and adopted him as a son.

sentences.zh: 少美容貌，好書史。

translations.literal: In youth he was handsome in appearance and fond of books and history.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was striking in appearance and devoted to books and history.

sentences.zh: 唐明宗先以女妻之，及即位，封其女為興平公主，拜延壽駙馬都尉、樞密使。

translations.literal: Tang Emperor Mingzong had first given him his daughter in marriage; when Mingzong took the throne he enfeoffed the daughter as Princess Xingping and appointed Yanshou Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant and Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingzong of Tang had already given him a daughter in marriage; once on the throne Mingzong ennobled the princess as Xingping and appointed Yanshou Imperial Son-in-Law Commandant and Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明宗子從榮恃權跋扈，內外莫不震懾，延壽求補外避之，出為宣武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Mingzong's son Congrong relied on power and acted overbearingly; within and without the court none were not awed, and Yanshou sought an outside appointment to avoid him, going out as Military Governor of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong's son Congrong abused his power and terrorized the court; Yanshou sought a provincial post to escape him and was sent out as military governor of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，加魯國公，復為樞密使，鎮許州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was made Duke of Lu, again became Commissioner of Military Affairs, and was stationed at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qingtai reign he was ennobled as Duke of Lu, returned to the post of Commissioner of Military Affairs, and took up his command at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭發兵太原，唐遣張敬達往討。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang raised troops at Taiyuan; Tang sent Zhang Jingda to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jingtang raised an army at Taiyuan, Tang dispatched Zhang Jingda to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 會敬達敗保晉安寨，延壽與德鈞往救，聞晉安已破，走團柏峪。

translations.literal: When Jingda was defeated and held Jin'an Stockade, Yanshou and Dejun went to the rescue; hearing that Jin'an had already fallen, they fled to Tuanbai Valley.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jingda was beaten back and bottled up at Jin'an Stockade, Yanshou and Dejun marched to relieve him; learning that Jin'an had already fallen, they retreated toward Tuanbai Valley.

sentences.zh: 太宗追及，延壽與其父俱降。

translations.literal: Taizong overtook them; Yanshou and his father both surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong caught up with them, and Yanshou surrendered together with his father.

sentences.zh: 明年，德鈞卒，以延壽為幽州節度使，封燕王。

translations.literal: The next year Dejun died; Yanshou was made Military Governor of Youzhou and enfeoffed as Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after Dejun's death, Yanshou was appointed military governor of Youzhou and enfeoffed as Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 及改幽州為南京，遷留守，總山南事。

translations.literal: When Youzhou was renamed the Southern Capital, he was transferred to be its garrison commander with overall charge of affairs south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhou was redesignated the Southern Capital, he was made its garrison commander with authority over all affairs south of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 天顯末，以延壽妻在晉，詔取之以歸。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianxian, because Yanshou's wife was in Jin, an edict ordered that she be brought back.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianxian era, because Yanshou's wife remained in Jin territory, an edict was issued to have her brought back to him.

sentences.zh: 自是益自激昂圖報。

translations.literal: From then on he became all the more ardent in plotting repayment.
translations.idiomatic: From that time on he burned with still greater zeal to repay the favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 會同初，帝幸其第，加政事令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong the emperor visited his residence and added the title Chief of Government Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huitong the emperor visited his home and additionally appointed him Chief of Government Affairs.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，晉人背盟，帝親征，延壽為先鋒，下貝州，授魏、博等州節度使，封魏王。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year the Jin violated the alliance; the emperor campaigned in person, with Yanshou as vanguard; he reduced Beizhou and was made Military Governor of Wei, Bo, and other prefectures, enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the sixth year, when Jin broke the treaty, the emperor marched in person with Yanshou in the vanguard; Yanshou took Beizhou, was made military governor of Wei, Bo, and neighboring prefectures, and was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 敗晉軍於南樂，獲其將賽項羽。

translations.literal: He defeated the Jin army at Nanle and captured their general Sai Xiangyu.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the Jin army at Nanle and took their general Sai Xiangyu prisoner.

sentences.zh: 軍元城，晉將李守貞、高行周率兵來逆，破之。

translations.literal: The army encamped at Yuancheng; the Jin generals Li Shouzhen and Gao Xingzhou led troops to oppose him, and he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Encamped at Yuancheng, he met and broke the Jin forces led by Li Shouzhen and Gao Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 至頓丘，會大霖雨，帝欲班師，延壽諫曰：「晉軍屯河濱，不敢出戰，若徑入澶州，奪其橋，則晉不足平。

translations.literal: Reaching Dunqiu, they encountered heavy rains; the emperor wished to withdraw the army. Yanshou remonstrated, saying: "The Jin army is encamped on the riverbank and dares not come out to fight; if we go straight into Chunzhou and seize its bridge, Jin will not be hard to pacify."
translations.idiomatic: At Dunqiu a torrential rain fell, and the emperor wanted to turn the army back. Yanshou urged him: "The Jin forces are camped along the river and dare not offer battle; if we strike straight for Chunzhou and seize its bridge, Jin will not be difficult to subdue."

sentences.zh: 」上然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 適晉軍先歸澶州，高行周至析城，延壽將輕兵逆戰；

translations.literal: Just then the Jin army had already returned to Chunzhou; Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng, and Yanshou led light troops to meet them in battle;
translations.idiomatic: By then the Jin army had already withdrawn to Chunzhou; when Gao Xingzhou reached Xicheng, Yanshou led light troops forward to give battle;

sentences.zh: 上親督騎士突其陣，敵遂潰。

translations.literal: the emperor personally directed the horsemen in a charge against their formation, and the enemy thereupon broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor himself directed the cavalry in a charge on their line, and the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 師還，留延壽徇貝、冀、深三州。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Yanshou was left to pacify the three prefectures of Bei, Ji, and Shen.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's withdrawal, Yanshou was left behind to secure the prefectures of Bei, Ji, and Shen.

sentences.zh: 八年，再伐晉，晉主遣延壽族人趙行實以書來招。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he campaigned against Jin again; the Jin ruler sent Yanshou's clansman Zhao Xingshi with a letter to entice him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, on the second expedition against Jin, the Jin emperor sent Yanshou's kinsman Zhao Xingshi with a letter inviting him to defect.

sentences.zh: 時晉人堅壁不出，延壽紿曰：「我陷虜久，寧忘父母之邦？

translations.literal: At the time the Jin held their walls and would not come out; Yanshou deceived them, saying: "I have long been trapped among the barbarians—how could I forget the land of my fathers?
translations.idiomatic: The Jin forces were holding their defenses and refusing battle; Yanshou feigned to them: "I have been captive among the Khitan so long—would I forget the land of my fathers?

sentences.zh: 若以軍逆，我即歸。

translations.literal: If you advance an army to meet me, I will at once return."
translations.idiomatic: Send an army to receive me, and I will come back at once."

sentences.zh: 」晉人以為然，遣杜重威率兵迎之。

translations.literal: " The Jin believed him and sent Du Chongwei at the head of troops to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Jin took him at his word and dispatched Du Chongwei with an army to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 延壽至滹沱河，據中渡橋，與晉軍力戰，手殺其將王清，兩軍相拒。

translations.literal: Yanshou reached the Hutuo River, held the Zhongdu Bridge, and fought the Jin army fiercely; with his own hand he killed their general Wang Qing, and the two armies stood locked in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou reached the Hutuo River, seized the Zhongdu Bridge, and fought the Jin army head on; he personally killed their commander Wang Qing, and the two sides remained locked in combat.

sentences.zh: 太宗潛由他渡濟，留延壽與耶律朔古據橋，敵不能奪，屢敗之，杜重威掃厥眾降。

translations.literal: Taizong secretly crossed by another ford; he left Yanshou and Yelu Shuogu to hold the bridge, which the enemy could not seize; they repeatedly defeated them, and Du Chongwei swept away his host in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong forded the river by another crossing in secret, leaving Yanshou and Yelu Shuogu to hold the bridge; the enemy could not take it, and after repeated defeats Du Chongwei surrendered with his entire force.

sentences.zh: 上喜，賜延壽龍鳳赭袍，且曰：「漢兵皆爾所有，爾宜親往撫慰。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, bestowed on Yanshou a dragon-and-phoenix scarlet robe, and said: "All these Han troops are now yours; you ought to go in person to reassure them."
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor granted Yanshou a dragon-and-phoenix scarlet robe and said: "All these Han soldiers are now under your command; you should go in person to reassure them."

sentences.zh: 」延壽至營，杜重威、李守貞迎謁馬首。

translations.literal: " When Yanshou reached the camp, Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen came to greet him at his horse's head.
translations.idiomatic: " When Yanshou arrived at the camp, Du Chongwei and Li Shouzhen came out to pay their respects at his stirrup.

sentences.zh: 高模翰，一名松，渤海人。

translations.literal: Gao Mohan, also named Song, was a man of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mohan, who also went by the name Song, was a native of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 有膂力，善騎射，好談兵。

translations.literal: He had great physical strength, excelled at mounted archery, and loved to discuss military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Powerfully built, he was a superb horseman and archer and loved to talk of war.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖平渤海，模翰避地高麗，王妻以女。

translations.literal: When Taizu first pacified Bohai, Mohan took refuge in Goryeo, and the king gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu first conquered Bohai, Mohan fled to Goryeo, where the king gave him a princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 因罪亡歸。

translations.literal: Because of a crime he fled and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After committing an offense he fled home again.

sentences.zh: 坐使酒殺人下獄，太祖知其才，貰之。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned for drunkenness and killing a man; Taizu knew his talent and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He was thrown into prison for killing a man while drunk; Taizu, recognizing his ability, pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 天顯十一年七月，唐遣張敬達、楊光遠帥師五十萬攻太原，勢銳甚。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eleventh year of Tianxian, Tang sent Zhang Jingda and Yang Guangyuan at the head of five hundred thousand troops to attack Taiyuan; their momentum was extremely sharp.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the eleventh year of Tianxian, Tang dispatched Zhang Jingda and Yang Guangyuan with an army said to number five hundred thousand against Taiyuan; their advance was ferocious.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭遣人求救，太宗許之。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang sent envoys to seek rescue; Taizong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang sent envoys to plead for aid, and Taizong agreed to march.

sentences.zh: 九月，征兵出雁門，模翰與敬達軍接戰，敗之，太原圍解。

translations.literal: In the ninth month troops were levied and marched out through Yanmen; Mohan joined battle with Jingda's army, defeated it, and the siege of Taiyuan was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the army marched out through Yanmen Pass; Mohan met Zhang Jingda in battle, routed him, and lifted the siege of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭夜出謁帝，約為父子。

translations.literal: Jingtang went out by night to pay court to the emperor and agreed to become father and son.
translations.idiomatic: That night Jingtang came out to pay homage to the emperor and agreed to enter a father-and-son relationship with him.

sentences.zh: 帝召模翰等賜以酒饌，親饗士卒，士氣益振。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Mohan and others, bestowed wine and food, and personally feasted the soldiers; morale rose still higher.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Mohan and the other commanders, treated them to food and wine, and personally entertained the troops, whose spirits soared.

sentences.zh: 翌日，復戰，又敗之。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again and defeated them once more.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they fought again and routed the Tang army a second time.

sentences.zh: 敬達鼠竄晉安寨，模翰獻俘於帝。

translations.literal: Jingda scurried like a rat into Jin'an Stockade; Mohan presented captives to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingda fled in disarray to Jin'an Stockade, and Mohan presented prisoners to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會敬瑭自立為晉帝，光遠斬敬達以降，諸州悉下。

translations.literal: When Jingtang declared himself Emperor of Jin, Guangyuan beheaded Jingda to surrender, and all the prefectures submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingtang proclaimed himself emperor of Jin, Yang Guangyuan killed Zhang Jingda and surrendered, and the prefectures fell one after another.

sentences.zh: 上諭模翰曰：「朕自起兵，百餘戰，卿功第一，雖古名將無以加。

translations.literal: The emperor addressed Mohan, saying: "Since I first raised the army, through more than a hundred battles your achievement ranks first; even the famous generals of antiquity cannot surpass it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Mohan: "Since I first took the field, in more than a hundred battles your merit has stood first; not even the great commanders of old could surpass it."

sentences.zh: 」乃授上將軍。

translations.literal: " He thereupon appointed him General-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: " He then appointed him General-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 會同元年，冊禮告成，宴百官及諸國使於二儀殿。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huitong, when the enthronement rites were completed, he feasted the hundred officials and envoys of the various states in the Hall of Two Principles.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huitong, when the investiture ceremonies were complete, he held a banquet for the officials and the envoys of foreign states in the Hall of Two Principles.

sentences.zh: 帝指模翰曰：「此國之勇將，朕統一天下，斯人之力也。

translations.literal: The emperor pointed to Mohan and said: "This is the valiant general of our state; in my unification of all under Heaven, it is this man's strength."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pointed to Mohan and said: "Here is the bravest general of the realm; in uniting the empire under my rule, it is to this man that I owe the most."

sentences.zh: 」群臣皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: " The assembled ministers all shouted "Long live the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: " The assembled ministers all cried "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 及晉叛盟，出師南伐。

translations.literal: When Jin broke the alliance, troops marched south to attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin violated the treaty, the army marched south on campaign.

sentences.zh: 模翰為統軍副使，與僧遏前驅，拔赤城，破德、貝諸寨。

translations.literal: Mohan served as deputy commander of the army; with Senge as vanguard he took Chicheng and stormed the stockades of De and Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Mohan served as deputy army commander; advancing with Senge as vanguard, he captured Chicheng and overran the fortified camps of De and Bei.

sentences.zh: 是冬，兼總左右鐵鷂子軍，下關南城邑數十。

translations.literal: That winter he also had overall command of the left and right Iron Hawk units and reduced several dozen walled places south of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he also took command of the left and right Iron Hawk corps and reduced several dozen towns south of the pass.

sentences.zh: 三月，敕虎官楊覃赴乾寧軍，為滄州節度使田武名所圍，模翰與趙延壽聚議往救。

translations.literal: In the third month the Tiger Guard officer Yang Tan was sent to Qianning Army and was besieged by Cangzhou Military Governor Tian Wuming; Mohan and Zhao Yanshou met in council to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Tiger Guard officer Yang Tan was posted to Qianning Army, where he was besieged by the military governor of Cangzhou, Tian Wuming; Mohan and Zhao Yanshou held council and agreed to march to his relief.

sentences.zh: 俄有光自模翰目中出，縈繞旗矛，焰焰如流星久之。

translations.literal: Suddenly a light issued from Mohan's eyes, coiled around flags and spears, and blazed like a meteor for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly a light shot from Mohan's eyes, wound about the banners and spears, and flared like a meteor for some time.

sentences.zh: 模翰喜曰：「此天贊之祥！

translations.literal: Mohan rejoiced and said: "This is a sign that Heaven approves!"
translations.idiomatic: Mohan exclaimed with joy: "This is Heaven's blessing upon us!"

sentences.zh: 」遂進兵，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: " He thereupon advanced the army and killed and captured in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: " He then pressed forward, killing and capturing a great many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 以功加侍中。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given the additional title Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was additionally appointed Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 略地鹽山，破饒安，晉人震怖，不敢接戰。

translations.literal: He overran the territory of Yanshan, stormed Rao'an, and the Jin were shaken with terror and dared not meet him in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He swept through Yanshan, took Rao'an, and the Jin were so terrified that they dared not offer battle.

sentences.zh: 加太傅。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 晉以魏府節度使杜重威領兵三十萬來拒，模翰謂左右曰：「軍法在正不在多。

translations.literal: Jin sent Wei prefectural Military Governor Du Chongwei at the head of three hundred thousand troops to resist; Mohan said to those beside him: "The art of war lies in righteousness, not in numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent the military governor of Wei, Du Chongwei, with an army said to number three hundred thousand to oppose him; Mohan told his attendants: "The art of war rests on justice, not on numbers.

sentences.zh: 以多陵少，不義必敗。

translations.literal: To use the many to overwhelm the few is unjust and must end in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: To overwhelm the few with the many is unjust and bound to end in defeat.

sentences.zh: 其晉之謂乎！

translations.literal: Is this not exactly Jin's case!"
translations.idiomatic: Is that not precisely Jin's situation?"

sentences.zh: 」詰旦，以麾下三百人逆戰，殺其先鋒梁漢璋，餘兵敗走。

translations.literal: " At dawn the next day he met the enemy with three hundred men under his command, killed their vanguard Liang Hanzhang, and the rest of the troops were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: " At dawn the next day he met them with three hundred men of his own command, killed their vanguard Liang Hanzhang, and put the rest to flight.

sentences.zh: 手詔褒美，比漢之李陵。

translations.literal: An imperial letter in the emperor's own hand praised him, comparing him to Han's Li Ling.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote him a personal commendation comparing him to Li Ling of Han.

sentences.zh: 頃之，杜重威等復至滹沱河，帝召模翰問計。

translations.literal: Before long Du Chongwei and the others again reached the Hutuo River; the emperor summoned Mohan to ask his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Du Chongwei and his forces again reached the Hutuo River, and the emperor called Mohan in to ask his counsel.

sentences.zh: 上善其言曰：「諸將莫及此。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and said: "None of the generals can match this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his plan and said: "None of the other commanders can equal this."

sentences.zh: 」乃令模翰守中渡橋。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Mohan to hold the Zhongdu Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: " He then ordered Mohan to defend the Zhongdu Bridge.

sentences.zh: 及戰，復敗之，上曰：「朕憑高觀兩軍之勢，顧卿英銳無敵，如鷹逐雉兔。

translations.literal: When battle was joined he defeated them again; the emperor said: "From on high I watched the momentum of the two armies; seeing your keen valor unmatched, it was like a hawk pursuing pheasant and hare.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting that followed he routed them again; the emperor said: "From the heights I watched the two armies contend; your fierce brilliance was unmatched—it was like a hawk stooping on pheasant and hare.

sentences.zh: 當圖形麟閣，爵貤後裔。

translations.literal: Your likeness should be painted in the Qilin Pavilion, and noble rank extended to your descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Your portrait should hang in the Qilin Pavilion, and ennoblement should pass to your descendants."

sentences.zh: 」已而杜重威等降。

translations.literal: " Before long Du Chongwei and the others surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward Du Chongwei and his command surrendered.

sentences.zh: 車駕入汴，加特進檢校太師，封悊郡開國公，賜璽書、劍器。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage entered Bian, Mohan was given the additional titles of Special Advancement and Acting Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of Te Commandery with state-founding rank, and bestowed an imperial letter under seal and a sword.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered Bian, Mohan was promoted to Special Advancement and Acting Grand Preceptor, enfeoffed as Duke of Te with state-founding rank, and granted an imperial letter under seal together with a ceremonial sword.

sentences.zh: 為汴州巡檢使，平汜水諸山土賊，遷鎮中京。

translations.literal: He served as Inspector of Bianzhou, pacified the mountain bandits around Sishui, and was transferred to garrison the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was made inspector of Bianzhou, suppressed the mountain bandits around Sishui, and was then transferred to command the garrison at the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 天祿二年，加開府儀同三司，賜對衣、鞍勒、名馬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianlu he was given the additional title of Grand General with the Ceremonies of an Imperial Scion, and was granted matching robes, saddle and bridle, and a famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianlu he was additionally appointed Grand General with Imperial Scion Ceremonies and presented with matching robes, saddle and bridle, and a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 應歷初，召為中臺省右相。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yingli he was summoned to be Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yingli reign he was recalled to serve as Right Chancellor of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至東京，父老歡迎曰：「公起戎行，致身富貴，為鄉里榮，相如、買臣輩不足過也。

translations.literal: When he reached the Eastern Capital, the elders welcomed him, saying: "You rose from the army to attain wealth and rank, bringing honor to our homeland—men like Sima Xiangru and Zhu Maichen cannot surpass you."
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the Eastern Capital, the local elders came out to welcome him, saying: "You rose from the ranks to wealth and high office and have brought glory to our home district—even figures like Sima Xiangru and Zhu Maichen could hardly outdo you."

sentences.zh: 」九年正月，遷左相，卒。

translations.literal: " In the first month of the ninth year he was transferred to Left Chancellor and died.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first month of the ninth year he was moved to Left Chancellor and died in office.

sentences.zh: 趙思溫，字文美，盧龍人。

translations.literal: Zhao Siwen, courtesy name Wenmei, was a native of Lulong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Siwen, whose courtesy name was Wenmei, came from Lulong.

sentences.zh: 少果銳，膂力兼人，隸燕帥劉仁恭幕。

translations.literal: In youth he was resolute and keen, with strength surpassing ordinary men, and served on the staff of the Yan commander Liu Rengong.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bold and decisive, with strength beyond that of ordinary men, and entered the staff of the Yan commander Liu Rengong.

sentences.zh: 李存勖問罪於燕，思溫統偏師拒之。

translations.literal: When Li Cunxu brought charges against Yan, Siwen commanded a detached force to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Cunxu marched against Yan, Siwen led a detached force to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 流矢中目，裂裳漬血，戰猶不已。

translations.literal: A stray arrow struck his eye; he tore his garment, blood soaking through, yet still would not cease fighting.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow struck his eye; he ripped his garment, blood soaking through, yet he would not stop fighting.

sentences.zh: 為存勖將周德威所擒，存勖壯而釋其縛。

translations.literal: He was captured by Cunxu's general Zhou Dewei; Cunxu admired his spirit and released his bonds.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei, a commander under Cunxu, took him prisoner; impressed by his courage, Cunxu had his bonds cut.

sentences.zh: 久之，日見信用。

translations.literal: After a long while he came to be trusted day by day.
translations.idiomatic: In time he won increasing trust.

sentences.zh: 與梁戰於莘縣，以驍勇聞，授平州刺史，兼平、營、薊三州都指揮使。

translations.literal: Fighting Liang at Shen county, he became known for fierce valor and was appointed Prefect of Pingzhou and overall commander of Ping, Ying, and Ji prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In battle with Liang at Shen county he won fame for fierce courage and was made prefect of Pingzhou and overall commander of Ping, Ying, and Ji.

sentences.zh: 神冊二年，太祖遣大將經略燕地，思溫來降。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shence, Taizu sent a great general to secure the Yan region; Siwen came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shence, when Taizu dispatched a senior commander to secure the Yan region, Siwen defected to Liao.

sentences.zh: 及伐渤海，以思溫為漢軍都團練使，力戰，拔扶餘城。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Bohai he was made Commander-in-Chief of the Han Army; fighting fiercely, he stormed Fuyu city.
translations.idiomatic: On the expedition against Bohai he was appointed commander-in-chief of the Han forces; after hard fighting he took Fuyu.

sentences.zh: 身被數創，太祖親為調藥。

translations.literal: His body received several wounds; Taizu personally prepared medicine for him.
translations.idiomatic: He suffered several wounds, and Taizu personally prepared medicine for him.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，以功擢檢校太保、保靜軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Taizong came to the throne, for his merit he was promoted to Acting Grand Guardian and Military Governor of Baojing.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's accession he was promoted for his service to Acting Grand Guardian and military governor of Baojing.

sentences.zh: 天顯十一年，唐兵攻太原，石敬瑭遣使求救，上命思溫自嵐、憲間出兵援之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Tianxian, Tang troops attacked Taiyuan; Shi Jingtang sent envoys to seek rescue, and the emperor ordered Siwen to march out between Lan and Xian to relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Tianxian, when Tang forces besieged Taiyuan, Shi Jingtang sent envoys to plead for aid; the emperor ordered Siwen to march from the Lan and Xian region to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 既罷兵，改南京留守、盧龍軍節度使、管內觀察處置等使、開府儀同三司，兼侍中，賜協謀靜亂翊聖功臣，尋改臨海軍節度使。

translations.literal: After the army was dismissed, he was made Garrison Commander of the Southern Capital, Military Governor of Lulong, Commissioner for Observation and Disposition within the circuit, Grand General with Imperial Scion Ceremonies, and concurrent Palace Attendant, granted the title of Meritorious Minister Who Assists in Planning to Pacify Disorder and Support the Sage; soon after he was transferred to Military Governor of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended he was appointed garrison commander of the Southern Capital, military governor of Lulong, and commissioner for observation and disposition within the circuit, with the additional titles of Grand General with Imperial Scion Ceremonies and Palace Attendant, and was granted the honorific of meritorious minister who assists in planning to pacify disorder; he was soon transferred to military governor of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 會同初，從耶律牒摐使晉行冊禮，還，加檢校太師。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong he followed Yelu Dieceng as envoy to Jin to perform the investiture rites; on his return he was given the additional title Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huitong he accompanied Yelu Dieceng on the mission to Jin to perform the enthronement ceremonies; on his return he was additionally appointed Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 二年，有星隕於庭，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year a star fell in his courtyard, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year a meteor fell in his courtyard, and he died.

sentences.zh: 上遣使賻祭，贈太師、魏國公。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys with funeral gifts and sacrifices, posthumously enfeoffing him as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys with funeral offerings and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Preceptor and Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 子延照、延靖，官至使相。

translations.literal: His sons Yanzhao and Yanjing rose to the rank of commissioner-chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Yanzhao and Yanjing both rose to commissioner-chancellor rank.

sentences.zh: 耶律漚裏思，六院夷離堇蒲古只之後。

translations.literal: Yelu Oulisi was a descendant of Pugu, Yelü chieftain of the Six Courts.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Oulisi was descended from Pugu, the Yelü chieftain of the Six Courts.

sentences.zh: 負勇略，每戰被重鎧，揮鐵槊，所向披靡。

translations.literal: He possessed courage and stratagem; in every battle he wore heavy armor and wielded an iron spear, scattering all before him.
translations.idiomatic: Endowed with courage and tactical skill, he went into battle in heavy armor, swinging an iron spear, and swept aside all who stood before him.

sentences.zh: 會同間，伐晉，上至河而獵，適海東青鶻搏雉，晉人隔水以鴿引去。

translations.literal: During Huitong, campaigning against Jin, the emperor reached the river on a hunt; just then a gyrfalcon from the eastern sea struck a pheasant, and the Jin across the water lured it away with a pigeon.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huitong campaigns against Jin, the emperor came to the river on a hunting excursion; a gyrfalcon from the eastern sea stooped on a pheasant, and men of Jin across the water lured the bird away with a carrier pigeon.

sentences.zh: 上顧左右曰：「誰為我得此人？

translations.literal: The emperor looked to those beside him and said: "Who will get this man for me?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to his attendants and asked: "Who will bring that man to me?"

sentences.zh: 」漚裏思請內廄馬，濟河擒之，並殺救者數人還。

translations.literal: " Oulisi requested a horse from the imperial stables, crossed the river, seized him, and killed several of the rescuers before returning.
translations.idiomatic: " Oulisi asked for a horse from the imperial stables, forded the river, seized the man, killed several of those who tried to rescue him, and returned.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，優加賞賚。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and rewarded him with exceptional bounty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and heaped rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 既而晉將杜重威逆於望都，據水勒戰。

translations.literal: Before long the Jin general Du Chongwei opposed them at Wangdu, holding the water and forcing battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Jin commander Du Chongwei met them at Wangdu, taking position along the water and forcing a battle.

sentences.zh: 漚裏思介馬突陣，余軍繼之。

translations.literal: Oulisi, armored on horseback, charged the formation, and the rest of the army followed.
translations.idiomatic: Oulisi, in full armor on horseback, smashed into the enemy line, and the rest of the army followed.

sentences.zh: 被圍，眾言陣薄處可出，漚裏思曰：「恐彼有他備。

translations.literal: Surrounded, the troops said a thin place in the formation offered escape; Oulisi said: "I fear they have another ambush there."
translations.idiomatic: When they were surrounded, his men pointed to a thin spot in the enemy line as a way out, but Oulisi said: "They may have another trap laid there."

sentences.zh: 」竟引兵沖堅而出；

translations.literal: " In the end he led his troops straight through the strongest point and broke out;
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he drove his men straight through the strongest part of the line and broke out;

sentences.zh: 回視眾所指，皆大塹也。

translations.literal: looking back at where the troops had pointed, they were all great trenches.
translations.idiomatic: and when he looked back at the spot his men had indicated, he saw that it was lined with deep trenches.

sentences.zh: 其料敵多此類。

translations.literal: His reading of the enemy was often of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His judgment of the enemy was often of this kind.

sentences.zh: 是年，總領敵烈皮室軍，坐私免部曲，奪官，卒。

translations.literal: That year he had overall command of the Dilie Pishi army; for privately releasing men from his command he was stripped of office and died.
translations.idiomatic: That year, while commanding the Dilie Pishi army, he was deprived of his post for privately dismissing men from his command and died shortly afterward.

sentences.zh: 張礪，磁州人，初仕唐為掌書記，遷翰林學士。

translations.literal: Zhang Li, a native of Cizhou, first served Tang as chief secretary and was transferred to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Li, a native of Cizhou, first served Tang as chief secretary and was later promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 會石敬瑭起兵，唐主以礪為招討判官，從趙德鈞援張敬達於河東。

translations.literal: When Shi Jingtang raised troops, the Tang ruler made Li staff judge of the punitive expedition, and he followed Zhao Dejun to relieve Zhang Jingda in Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Jingtang rebelled, the Tang emperor appointed Li staff judge on the punitive campaign, and he accompanied Zhao Dejun to relieve Zhang Jingda in Hedong.

sentences.zh: 及敬達敗，礪入契丹。

translations.literal: When Jingda was defeated, Li entered Khitan territory.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingda's defeat, Li went over to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 後太宗見礪剛直有文彩，擢翰林學士。

translations.literal: Later Taizong saw that Li was upright and gifted in letters and promoted him to Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizong, seeing that Li was upright and accomplished in letters, appointed him Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 礪臨事必盡言，無所避，上益重之。

translations.literal: In office Li always spoke his full mind without evasion, and the emperor valued him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: In office Li spoke his mind fully and held nothing back, and the emperor came to esteem him still more.

sentences.zh: 未幾，謀亡歸，為追騎所獲。

translations.literal: Before long he plotted to flee home and was seized by pursuing horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he plotted to escape and return home, but was caught by pursuing horsemen.

sentences.zh: 上責曰：「汝何故亡？

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him, saying: "Why did you flee?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reproached him: "Why did you run away?"

sentences.zh: 」礪對曰：「臣不習北方土俗，飲食居處，意常郁郁，以是亡耳。

translations.literal: " Li replied: "Your servant is unaccustomed to northern customs in food, drink, and dwelling; my mind was always depressed, and for that reason I fled."
translations.idiomatic: " Li answered: "I am unused to northern ways of eating, drinking, and living; I was constantly depressed, and that is why I fled."

sentences.zh: 」上顧通事高彥英曰：「朕嘗戒汝善遇此人，何乃使失所而亡？

translations.literal: " The emperor turned to the interpreter Gao Yan'ying and said: "I once warned you to treat this man well—how could you let him lose his footing and flee?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor turned to the interpreter Gao Yan'ying and said: "I once told you to treat this man well—how did you let him become so miserable that he fled?

sentences.zh: 礪去，可再得耶？

translations.literal: If Li is gone, can he be obtained again?"
translations.idiomatic: If Li were lost, could we ever find his like again?"

sentences.zh: 」遂杖彥英而謝礪。

translations.literal: " He thereupon had Yan'ying beaten with the staff and apologized to Li.
translations.idiomatic: " He then had Yan'ying beaten and apologized to Li.

sentences.zh: 會同初，升翰林承旨，兼吏部尚書，從太宗伐晉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huitong he was promoted to Hanlin Academician Expositor, concurrent Minister of Personnel, and followed Taizong in the campaign against Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Huitong he was promoted to chief Hanlin academician and concurrent minister of personnel, and accompanied Taizong on the campaign against Jin.

sentences.zh: 入汴，諸將蕭翰、耶律郎五、麻答輩肆殺掠，礪奏曰：「今大遼始得中國，宜以中國人治之，不可專用國人及左右近習。

translations.literal: On entering Bian, the generals Xiao Han, Yelu Langwu, Mada, and their like indulged in killing and plunder; Li memorialized, saying: "Now that Great Liao has just obtained China, China ought to be governed by Chinese; one cannot rely solely on our countrymen and close attendants."
translations.idiomatic: After entering Bian, generals such as Xiao Han, Yelu Langwu, and Mada ran wild with killing and looting; Li submitted a memorial saying: "Now that Great Liao has only just taken possession of China, China should be governed by Chinese; the court cannot rely solely on Khitan and on those close at hand."

sentences.zh: 茍政令乖失，則人心不服，雖得之亦將失之。

translations.literal: If policies and orders go astray, hearts will not submit; though you have gained it, you will yet lose it.
translations.idiomatic: If government and orders go wrong, the people will not submit; even what has been won will soon be lost again.

sentences.zh: 」上不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 改右僕射，兼門下侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: He was made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with concurrent posts as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 頃之，車駕北還，至欒城崩。

translations.literal: Before long the imperial carriage returned north; at Luancheng the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor turned north; at Luancheng he died.

sentences.zh: 時礪在恒州，蕭翰與麻答以兵圍其第。

translations.literal: At the time Li was at Hengzhou; Xiao Han and Mada surrounded his residence with troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li was then at Hengzhou; Xiao Han and Mada surrounded his house with soldiers.

sentences.zh: 礪方臥病，出見之。

translations.literal: Li was then ill in bed but went out to see them.
translations.idiomatic: Though Li was ill in bed, he went out to face them.

sentences.zh: 翰數之曰：「汝何故於先帝言國人不可為節度使？

translations.literal: Han reproached him, saying: "Why did you tell the late emperor that our countrymen could not serve as military governors?"
translations.idiomatic: Han denounced him: "Why did you tell the late emperor that Khitan could not be made military governors?"

sentences.zh: 我以國舅之親，有征伐功，先帝留我守汴，以為宣武軍節度使，汝獨以為不可。

translations.literal: I am kin to the emperor as maternal uncle, with merit in campaigns; the late emperor left me to hold Bian and made me Military Governor of Xuanwu—you alone said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: I am the emperor's uncle by marriage and have earned merit in war; the late emperor left me to guard Bian and made me military governor of Xuanwu—you alone said that was wrong.

sentences.zh: 又譖我與解裏好掠人財物子女。

translations.literal: You also slandered me and Jieli as fond of seizing people's goods and daughters.
translations.idiomatic: You also accused me and Jieli of plundering people's goods and taking their women.

sentences.zh: 今必殺汝！

translations.literal: Today I shall certainly kill you!"
translations.idiomatic: Today I will kill you!"

sentences.zh: 」趣令鎖之。

translations.literal: " He hurriedly ordered him bound.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered him bound at once.

sentences.zh: 礪抗聲曰：「此國家大體，安危所系，吾實言之。

translations.literal: Li answered in a ringing voice: "This concerns the great principles of the state and what binds its safety and peril—I spoke the truth of it.
translations.idiomatic: Li answered boldly: "This touches the fundamental interests of the state and its safety—I spoke only the truth.

sentences.zh: 欲殺即殺，奚以鎖為？

translations.literal: If you wish to kill, then kill—why bind me?"
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to kill me, then kill me—why bother to bind me?"

sentences.zh: 」麻答以礪大臣，不可專殺，乃救止之。

translations.literal: " Mada, considering Li a great minister who could not be killed on private authority, thereupon restrained Han and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: " Mada, holding that a senior minister could not be killed on a private grudge, intervened and stopped him.

sentences.zh: 是夕，礪恚憤卒。

translations.literal: That night Li died of indignant rage.
translations.idiomatic: That night Li died of grief and anger.

sentences.zh: 論曰：初，晉因遼之兵而得天下，故兼臣禮而父事之，割地以為壽，輸帛以為貢。

translations.literal: The commentators say: At first Jin obtained the realm through Liao's troops; therefore it observed both the rites of a subject and treated Liao as a father, ceding territory as a gift of longevity and sending silks as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: At first Jin had won the empire with Liao's armies; it therefore observed the rites of a subject while treating Liao as a father, ceding territory as a gift and sending silk as tribute.

sentences.zh: 未久也，而會同之師次滹沱矣。

translations.literal: Not long after, the armies of Huitong halted at the Hutuo.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, the armies of Huitong were encamped at the Hutuo River.

sentences.zh: 豈群帥貪功黷武而致然歟？

translations.literal: Was this because the commanders in their greed for merit abused military force?
translations.idiomatic: Was this because the commanders, greedy for glory, abused military force?

sentences.zh: 抑所謂信不由衷也哉？

translations.literal: Or was it rather what is called faith not proceeding from the heart?
translations.idiomatic: Or was it, as the saying goes, that their pledge of faith never came from the heart?

sentences.zh: 模翰以功名自終，可謂良將。

translations.literal: Mohan ended his life in merit and fame and may be called a good general.
translations.idiomatic: Mohan ended his career in honor and may truly be called a fine general.

sentences.zh: 若延壽之勛雖著，至於覬覦儲位，謬矣，利令智昏，固無足議。

translations.literal: As for Yanshou, though his achievements were conspicuous, in coveting the heir's position he erred; profit blinded his judgment—there is truly nothing worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou's achievements were great, but in coveting the throne he was deluded; gain had blinded his judgment, and he is hardly worth further discussion.

sentences.zh: 若乃成末釁以虧俊功，如解裏者，何譏焉！

translations.literal: As for allowing a final blemish to mar outstanding achievement, like Jieli—what reproach is there?!
translations.idiomatic: As for letting a late misstep tarnish a fine record, as with Jieli—what is there to blame?!
